text:
Jordan: seeing a small but reproducible correctness regression on kv pages in prod after the rollout. different user gets tokens that belong to prior request :/
Mia: ack, saw a support case too. any repro?
Jordan: yes — long-context chat (>8k) + simultaneous small requests. after a few minutes p95 responses start showing extra tokens that match earlier prompts.
Ashwin: do we have logs showing page reuse / eviction timing?
Jordan: dumping a sample:
```
[2026-02-21T14:02:41Z] kv_page: id=42 slot=7 owner_req_id=req-8f3a evict_ts=1700 used=0x3f tag=0x1a9f checksum=0x7c12
[2026-02-21T14:02:41Z] kv_page: id=42 slot=7 owner_req_id=req-a12b used=0x01 tag=0x1a9f checksum=0x7c12
[2026-02-21T14:02:43Z] generate: resp=req-c33b tokens=... (contains remnants from req-8f3a)
```
Lucy: owner_req_id is supposed to be cleared on evict. looks like eviction path didn't reset owner for some fast-rotate paths.
Ashwin: this smells like our recent prefetch + tail-merge optimization where we append to an existing page if free_space > threshold. might be skipping full zeroing for perf.
Mia: Perf team flagged a ~3% token-generation improvement with the skipping, but correctness beats perf here.
Jordan: repro script (local):
```bash
# run long context worker in background
python repro_long_context.py --length 9500 &
# hammer with small requests in parallel
for i in {1..250}; do curl -sS -X POST /generate -d '{"prompt":"ping $i"}' & done
```
Ashwin: I ran perf counters — at time of contamination evict_count spikes but page_release_callbacks are lower than expected. suspect callback not invoked on fast-path free.
PerfBot: perf snapshot attached: cpu_cycles +12%, cache-misses +2%, page_release_misses=17 (expected <3)
Lucy: Also saw non-matching checksum sometimes identical across two different owners. maybe checksum computed before tag update.
Jordan: Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) roll back prefetch append fast-path (cheap revert) 2) add assert in debug builds that validates page.owner_req_id cleared on reuse 3) server-side hotfix to zero owner_req_id and tag on reassign (safest).
Mia: agree. For longer-term: add per-block incremental checksum that includes request-id and a 16-bit epoch so we can detect cross-request contamination at read time and auto-fail instead of serving corrupted tokens.
Ashwin: implementation notes: computing 16-bit checksum for a 4KB block is cheap (crc16). We can store checksum in page header and validate when rehydrating KV into GPU memory. If mismatch, drop and treat as miss.
Lucy: what about cost of zeroing vs checksum? zeroing costs memory bandwidth on allocation, checksum costs compute on every write and read. but checksum allows lazy validation.
Jordan: rollout plan I propose:
- revert fast-path in canary for 1 hour -> watch error rate and contamination alerts
- add debug assertion + telemetry (page_reassign_without_clear counter)
- schedule checksum change in next minor release with opt-in flag

Ashwin: I'll open a PR for the revert + asserts now. Mia can you add an alert for any generate responses that match tokens from a different req-id within 1s? cheap heuristic.
Mia: on it. also adding a temporary blocklist: if contamination detected on a page id, mark page as quarantined and evict ASAP.
CI Bot: build queued for branch: revert/kv-fastpath-2026-02-21 #4579
Jordan: thanks. can we also add a perf benchmark to measure impact of revert (microbench: kv-alloc/free throughput + end-to-end p99 gen)?
PerfBot: benchmark job queued: kv-fastpath-revert-bench (ETA 22m)
Ashwin: PR link once ready — will include changelog and a small unit test that simulates parallel long-context + small-req rotation and asserts no cross-request tokens.
Lucy: good. also add tracing tag to pages: trace/page_id and include in logs for easier postmortem.
Jordan: TL;DR: suspected reused page with stale owner tag after fast-path append. immediate revert + telemetry, medium-term checksum/quarantine path. thanks team :thumbsup:
